crit: The selected imbalanced datasets are publicly available from the UCI and KEEL repositories; to test the algorithm on more extreme cases of imbalance, undersampled modifications (initial IR multiplied by 2 and 3) and simulated binary imbalanced data (variations of MADELON) were added, for 69 datasets; an undersampled dataset was used only if it kept at least 15 minority samples.
notes: The paper never describes how natively multiclass sources were made two-class and never says which datasets come from UCI vs KEEL. Binarised/repository/repository-defined rest on the KEEL-style split names in Table 1 (NEW THYROID 1/2, YEAST 1/3/4/5/6, PAGE BLOCKS 0, PAGE BLOCKS 1 3). Several natively multiclass datasets appear as two-class with no split suffix (IRIS, WINE, GLASS, VEHICLE, ECOLI, BREAST TISSUE, EUCALYPTUS, SEGMENTATION, VOWEL, LED, LIBRAS, DERMATOLOGY); if any of these came from UCI, the authors must have binarised them, and binarised_by would be 'both' and minority_rule 'not stated'. Adjudicator should check. Count mismatch: text says 13 UCI + 13 KEEL + 2 simulated = 28 base datasets, but Table 1 has 27 base names (25 real + MANDELON 1 and 2) in 69 rows. 'MANDELON' is printed for MADELON throughout. 'Publicly available' is stated but not as a selection reason, so replicability was not coded. Generated = the two simulated MADELON-variation datasets (generator of Guyon 2003). Table 1 prints no class count (all two-class: minority/majority instances). No per-dataset results in the paper: Tables 2-3 give means/ranks across datasets; full results only on GitHub. Experiment scripts also on GitHub.
